chunks: What Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Abī Jamīlah, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who died while in a place where there was no other woman with them besides her. He said to him: If there is not among them her husband or a mahram relative of hers, they should bury her in her clothes and not perform ghusl for her. But if her husband or a mahram relative of hers is with them, then he should perform ghusl for her without looking at her ʿawrah.

He said: And I asked him about a man who died while traveling with women, and there was no man with them. So he said: If he does not have a wife among them, then he should be buried in his clothes and not be given ghusl. But if he has a wife among them, then he should be given ghusl while wearing a shirt, without looking at his ʿawrah.

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the condition in which this ruling occurs
key_terms.بِثِيَابِهَا: in her clothes, without removing them
key_terms.ذُو رَحِمٍ: a blood relative within the unmarriageable kinship relationship
key_terms.عَوْرَتِهَا: her private parts that must not be looked at
key_terms.قَمِيصٍ: a shirt used to preserve covering during ghusl
key_terms.يُغَسِّلُونَهَا: they perform ghusl for her body after death

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man or woman dies during travel and only unrelated members of the opposite sex are present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings for washing and burying the dead when a person dies in travel and only unrelated members of the opposite sex are present. It states that if no spouse or mahram relative is present, the deceased is buried in their clothes without ghusl; if a spouse or mahram is present, ghusl may be performed while preserving the covering of the ʿawrah.
